reasoning: A discontinuous circumfix, ma before the verb and an unstressed -sh suffixed to it: ma ba3rafsh, ma bakulsh. The dots cannot be romanized, so only the two pieces are written.
English 'block' taken in as a form II verb, ballakni he blocked me. Young Ramallah speakers also say 3imil-li block, so the verb form is current but not the only option.
A learned word with no colloquial rival, so Palestinians keep the ث here rather than shifting it to t as in native words. Some speakers say talawwus.
ث becomes t in this everyday word, like thaalith to taalit, so it is respelled تانية. Taa marbuta after ي is e.
Word-initial hamza on an alif seat is not written, so the romanization starts with the vowel ee. Everyday Ramallah question word for when.

romanization: illi byijri wara id-dinya ma byil7a'ha
vowelled_arabic: اللِّي بْيِجْرِي وَرَا الدُّنْيَا مَا بْيِلْحَقْها
reasoning: Dialectal relative illi plus the b- present byijri, byil7a'. ق in يلحق is a glottal stop, and il- assimilates to the sun letter د in id-dinya.
The MSA diphthong aw is a long oo in Palestinian, so موسم is said moosim and respelled with waw plus damma. Used for the olive and fruit seasons and for any season of activity.
In learned words ذ comes out as z in urban Palestinian, so jazzaab, respelled with ز; the d realisation jaddaab is also heard. Shadda on the middle radical doubles it.
b- present with the you-m. prefix bt-, and ween for where. The frame ends on the article il-, which is what the slot attaches to.
A place name; the final hamza of الصحراء is dropped in speech. il- assimilates to the sun letter ص and stays il- before the moon letter غ.

meaning_fix: carbonated / fizzy (adjective); the drink is مشروب غازي
reasoning: غازي on its own is the adjective carbonated, not a noun for soda. Palestinians order a mashruub ghaazi or just name the brand.
In the construct the taa marbuta of مرة is pronounced t and the vowel drops: mart 3amm. Standard Ramallah kinship term for the paternal uncle's wife.
Everyday market phrase. keelo has ee then a final o, not uu.
اعتصام is specifically a sit-in or stationary vigil; a general protest or march is مظاهرة. Word-initial hamza on the alif seat is not romanized.
Said with the initial cluster 7saab, and often shortened to 3a 7saabi in fast speech. Normal Ramallah way to offer to pay.
English loan used as a noun, 3milli foolo give me a follow. Both syllables have rounded back vowels; the first is the stressed long one.
The short counting form used directly before a noun, tis3 banaat, as against tis3a standing alone. A linking t appears before vowel-initial nouns, tis3t iyyaam.
Form II passive participle from قلم, with ق as a glottal stop and a shadda doubling the lam. Used of striped cloth.
ط is emphatic, hence the capital T. Covers both simple or easy and, of a person, easygoing; also 'it's nothing' in basiiTa.
Word-initial hamza seat is not written, so ibn. Taa marbuta after م is e, and the shadda doubles the mim.
ق in حرق is a glottal stop and the conjunction fuses with the article as wil-. The idiom is pan-Arab rather than specifically Palestinian, but a Ramallah speaker uses it as is.
Form II participle with an initial cluster, emphatic ط as T and ق as a glottal stop. Feminine is mTalla'a.
Derived from burt'aan oranges, with ق as a glottal stop; some Ramallah speakers voice the t and say burd'aani. The colour adjective, not the fruit.
Palestinian raises the first vowel of this pattern to i: nija7, not najaha. Used both for succeeding generally and for passing an exam.
il- assimilates to the sun letter ص. A money-changing term Ramallah speakers use daily given the shekel, dinar and dollar.
